title: Execution of James, brother of Jesus, by order of the high priest Ananus
summary: According to Josephus, the high priest Ananus, son of Ananus, convened the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem in the gap between the death of the procurator Festus and the arrival of Albinus. He had James, called the brother of Jesus, and others stoned as lawbreakers. Ananus was afterwards removed from office.

uncertainty.note: Josephus gives no calendar year; 62 CE is the reference source's dating of Albinus's procuratorship.

as_recorded.value: Festus was now dead, and Albinus was but upon the road (no calendar year given)

as_recorded.calendar: Year supplied by the reference source

where.historical_name: Jerusalem, Roman province of Judaea under procurators

importance.justification: One of the few non-Christian accounts naming a leader of the early Jesus movement, and an illustration of tension between the Jerusalem priesthood and Roman authority.

sources.title: The Antiquities of the Jews, 20.197–20.200 (Whiston translation)
sources.author: Flavius Josephus

reviewer_note: Year 62 is inferred from the date given for Albinus; the passage itself is undated. Some scholars dispute the phrase identifying James as brother of Jesus; later Christian traditions of his death differ and were not opened. A stub exists at 0062-execution-of-james-brother-of-jesus that may be the same event.
